habitat: Marshes, damp valleys and vleis, concealed in dense vegetation. It seldom overlaps Buff-spotted Flufftail in habitat.
summary: A fairly common resident. Very similar to Buff-spotted Flufftail. The male's reddish colour extends onto the mantle and lower breast, the tail is mostly black, and the upperparts are streaked rather than spotted. The female is much darker, but paler on the chest and throat. The usual call is a repeated ooo-ooo-ooo-ooo-dueh. The Kemp name Redchested Flufftail and the code VB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Buff-spotted Flufftail has rounded buff spots, a chestnut tail barred black, and lives in forest and long grass rather than marsh.

calls.description: The usual call is a much-repeated 'ooo-ooo-ooo-ooo-duehdueh-dueh…'. It also gives a quail-like 'ick-kick-kick-kick…' and a loud rapid 'dui-dui-dui…' up to 40 times, fading at the end. The grade A call, with wind noise, is from near Klerksdorp. No Kruger recording was found. The filename is XC645330-5%20Good%20RC%20F%20Tail%20with%20wind.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a fairly common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. No Kruger photograph was found under an allowed licence. A male side photograph from the Garden Route is stored. The grade A call is from North West and includes wind noise. The Kemp name Redchested Flufftail and the code VB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^5=32 mature individuals (visiting breeder); paper interval half–double → 16–64.
